questions.prompt: A hospital trust plans to migrate patient records to a third-party cloud provider based overseas. Discuss the legal and ethical issues the trust must consider before proceeding.

levels.title: Level 3 (High Mark Band)
levels.ao1: Comprehensive, accurate technical knowledge using correct terminology throughout.
levels.ao2: Thorough application to the scenario with coherent, logical progression of ideas.
levels.ao3: Critical, balanced evaluation; arguments substantiated and a reasoned conclusion drawn.

levels.title: Level 2 (Medium Mark Band)
levels.ao1: Sound knowledge of concepts with mostly correct terminology.
levels.ao2: Application to the context is present but uneven or partially developed.
levels.ao3: Some evaluation; arguments one-sided or conclusions asserted rather than reasoned.

levels.title: Level 1 (Low Mark Band)
levels.ao1: Basic knowledge; isolated facts or terminology with occasional inaccuracy.
levels.ao2: Superficial or generic application; little reference to the actual scenario.
levels.ao3: Little or no evaluation; opinion without justification.

indicativeContent: Data Protection Act 2018 / UK GDPR principles: lawfulness, purpose limitation, data minimisation
Rights of data subjects (access, erasure) and how outsourcing affects them
International transfer rules — adequacy, safeguards, or explicit consent required for overseas processing
Security obligations: encryption in transit/at rest, breach notification within 72 hours
Ethical duties beyond law: patient trust, re-identification risk from pseudonymised data
Accountability: the trust remains data controller even when processing is outsourced
Balanced conclusion weighing clinical/operational benefits against privacy risk

questions.prompt: A logistics company processes delivery routes on datasets that are nearly sorted, with occasional new insertions. Evaluate whether insertion sort, merge sort, or quicksort is the best choice for their routing system, justifying your recommendation.

indicativeContent: Insertion sort is O(n) on nearly-sorted input — adaptive behaviour suits this exact data profile
Merge sort guarantees O(n log n) regardless of input but costs O(n) extra memory
Quicksort averages O(n log n) but degrades to O(n²) on sorted/nearly-sorted data with naive pivot choice
Insertion sort's low overhead and in-place operation suit small-to-medium route lists
For large datasets the quadratic worst case of insertion sort may dominate — dataset size matters
Stability may matter if equal-priority deliveries must keep original ordering
Justified recommendation tied to the scenario's stated characteristics

indicativeContent: The problem is a travelling salesman variant — exact brute force is factorial and intractable at n=20
Abstraction: road network as weighted graph, irrelevant detail (vehicle colour, road names) discarded
Heuristics trade optimality for tractability — nearest neighbour, or A* with straight-line distance heuristic
Decomposition into route representation, cost evaluation, improvement steps
Evaluation: whether 'good enough' routes suffice commercially versus guaranteed-optimal cost
Reasoned conclusion about acceptable approximation in practice
